cues.en: Check this out. I'm using this speaker to vibrate a petri dish containing silicone oil. Now if I take this toothpick and I make a little droplet on the surface,
cues.zh: 看这个。我用这个扬声器振动一个装有硅油的培养皿。现在如果我拿这根牙签，在表面弄出一个小液滴，

cues.en: the droplet will stay there hovering above the surface.
cues.zh: 液滴会悬停在表面上方不动。

cues.en: The droplet is actually bouncing,
cues.zh: 液滴其实在弹跳，

cues.en: and it'll keep bouncing for a very long time.
cues.zh: 而且会弹跳很长时间。

cues.en: Now the reason for this is there's a little layer of air between the droplet and the surface, and the droplet's bouncing so rapidly that that layer never shrinks to about a 100 nanometers, which is what it would take for the droplet to recombine with the oil.
cues.zh: 原因是液滴和表面之间有一薄层空气，液滴弹跳得太快，这层空气始终不会缩小到大约100纳米，而液滴要与油重新融合就需要缩到那个程度。

cues.en: Now every time the droplet lands on the surface, it creates a wave.
cues.zh: 每次液滴落到表面，都会产生一道波。

cues.en: But this is a special type of wave driven by the vibration of the oil bath.
cues.zh: 但这是一种特殊的波，由油浴的振动驱动。

cues.en: It is a standing wave, meaning that it's not traveling out. It's just oscillating up and down.
cues.zh: 它是驻波，意思是它不会向外传播，只是在原地上下振荡。

cues.en: So the droplet makes the wave, and then it interacts with that wave on its next bounce.
cues.zh: 所以液滴产生波，然后在下次弹跳时与那道波相互作用。

cues.en: If the drop lands on one side of the wave, it is pushed forwards. And as long as the bounce of the droplet remains synchronized with the wave, it'll keep landing on the front side of the wave and getting pushed farther forwards.
cues.zh: 如果液滴落在波的一侧，它就会被向前推。只要液滴的弹跳与波保持同步，它就会一直落在波的前侧，并被推得越来越远。

cues.en: Droplets like these are known as walkers.
cues.zh: 这样的液滴被称为行走液滴。

cues.en: The bouncing oil drops have been known about since the nineteen seventies, but only recently has it been discovered that you can use these little droplets to replicate many of the strange phenomena of quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 弹跳的油滴早在20世纪70年代就为人所知，但直到最近才发现，可以用这些小液滴来复现量子力学的许多奇特现象。

cues.en: Now, obviously, this is not a quantum system. The droplets are about a millimeter in diameter. But you can think of the droplets like
cues.zh: 很显然，这并不是量子系统。液滴直径大约有一毫米。但你可以把这些液滴想象成

cues.en: quantum particles, say, electrons.
cues.zh: 量子粒子，比如电子。

cues.en: One experiment that captures the key features of quantum mechanics is the double slit experiment.
cues.zh: 能体现量子力学核心特征的一个实验，就是双缝实验。

cues.en: If you send a beam of electrons at two narrow slits, well, the electrons, rather than behaving like particles and ending up in two clumps behind the slits,
cues.zh: 如果向两条狭缝发射一束电子，电子并不会表现得像经典粒子那样在缝后形成两堆，

cues.en: they produce an interference pattern even when you send each electron through one at a time.
cues.zh: 而是会产生干涉图样，即使你每次只发射一个电子也是如此。

cues.en: With walking droplets, the pilot wave goes through both slits interfering with itself, while the droplet only goes through one slit. The droplet doesn't move in a straight line, though. It's deflected by its interaction with the wave.
cues.zh: 而在行走的液滴实验中，导波会穿过两条狭缝并发生自我干涉，而液滴只穿过一条狭缝。不过液滴走的并不是直线，它因与波的相互作用而发生了偏转。

cues.en: The resulting distribution of where the droplets end up looks very similar to quantum double slit interference patterns. Or take tunneling.
cues.zh: 液滴最终落点的分布情况，看起来和量子双缝干涉图样非常相似。再来看隧穿效应。

cues.en: In quantum mechanics, it's possible for a particle to get through a barrier that it wouldn't classically have enough energy to get over. This has been demonstrated with walkers by creating a shallow barrier under the surface of the oil.
cues.zh: 在量子力学中，粒子有可能穿透在经典力学中因能量不足而无法翻越的势垒。通过在油面下方设置一个浅滩势垒，行走的液滴也演示了这一现象。

cues.en: Usually, the barrier reflects the pilot wave and its bouncing droplet. But in rare cases, the droplet does cross the boundary.
cues.zh: 通常情况下，势垒会反射导波以及弹跳的液滴。但在极少数情况下，液滴确实能穿过这个边界。

cues.en: And the probability of the droplet crossing the barrier decreases exponentially
cues.zh: 而且液滴穿过势垒的概率

cues.en: with the increasing width of the barrier just as in quantum tunneling. Perhaps the most surprising thing about these walkers is they exhibit quantization
cues.zh: 会随着势垒宽度的增加呈指数级下降，这和量子隧穿如出一辙。关于这些行走液滴，最令人惊奇的或许是它们展现出的量子化特征，

cues.en: just like electrons bound to atoms. Here the walker is confined to a circular corral. The droplet seems to move around randomly as it interacts with its pilot wave. The complex interaction between the droplet and the wave leads to chaotic motion of the droplet.
cues.zh: 就像束缚在原子内部的电子一样。这里液滴被限制在一个圆形围栏中。液滴在与自身的导波相互作用时，看起来像是在随机移动。液滴与波之间复杂的相互作用，导致了液滴呈现混沌运动。

cues.en: But over time, a pattern builds up.
cues.zh: 但随着时间推移，一种模式逐渐显现出来。

cues.en: This is probability density of finding the droplet at any point within the corral,
cues.zh: 这是在小围栏内任意一点找到液滴的概率密度，

cues.en: and it looks very similar to the probability density of electrons confined in a quantum corral.
cues.zh: 它看起来和电子被限制在量子围栏中的概率密度非常相似。

cues.en: All of these similarities are no coincidence.
cues.zh: 所有这些相似之处绝非巧合。

cues.en: The walking droplets actually create a remarkable physical realization of a theory proposed by de Broglie nearly a hundred years ago in the early days of quantum mechanics. He postulated that all particles have a wave that accompanies them and guides their motion, And that wave is actually created by tiny oscillations of the particle.
cues.zh: 行走液滴实际上惊人地实现了德布罗意在近百年前量子力学早期提出的一种理论。他假设所有粒子都有一个伴随并引导其运动的波，而这个波实际上是由粒子的微小振荡产生的。

cues.en: Now this pilot wave theory was marginalized
cues.zh: 后来，这种导波理论被边缘化了，

cues.en: when the standard Copenhagen interpretation became widely adopted.
cues.zh: 因为标准的哥本哈根诠释被广泛接受。

cues.en: The Copenhagen interpretation
cues.zh: 哥本哈根诠释

cues.en: excludes anything that cannot be directly observed.
cues.zh: 排除了任何无法直接观测的事物。

cues.en: And it says everything that can be known about a particle is contained in its so called wave function.
cues.zh: 它认为关于一个粒子所有可知的信息都包含在其所谓的波函数中。

cues.en: But adopting this view forces you to give up on some common sense notions like the idea that particles have a definite position and momentum even when they're not being measured. And it also meant that the universe was no longer deterministic.
cues.zh: 但采纳这种观点迫使你放弃一些常识性概念，比如粒子即使未被测量也具有确定位置和动量的想法。这也意味着宇宙不再是决定论的。

cues.en: Randomness is built into standard quantum mechanics. For example, take the double slit experiment. According to quantum mechanics, the wave function of the electron is a superposition of the electron going through one slit and the other slit simultaneously.
cues.zh: 随机性是标准量子力学固有的一部分。例如，拿双缝实验来说。根据量子力学，电子的波函数是电子同时通过一条缝和另一条缝的叠加态。

cues.en: Using this wave function, you can calculate the probability of where the electron is likely to be. And then when you detect it at the screen, the electron pops up at one point at random that was in that distribution.
cues.zh: 利用这个波函数，你可以计算电子可能出现位置的概率。然后当你在屏幕上探测它时，电子会随机地出现在该分布中的某一点上。

cues.en: We say that its wave function collapses instantaneously
cues.zh: 我们说它的波函数瞬间坍缩

cues.en: at the moment of measurement.
cues.zh: 在测量的那一刻。

cues.en: You can't say that the electron was there before you measured it, and you can't even say that the electron must have gone through one slit or the other. Compare that with the picture provided by the bouncing droplets. In this case, the pilot wave goes through both slits, but the droplet only goes through one.
cues.zh: 你不能说电子在测量之前就在那里，你甚至不能说电子一定穿过了某一条缝。将其与弹跳液滴所提供的图景进行比较。在这种情况下，导波穿过两条缝，但液滴只穿过一条。

cues.en: Droplet is pushed around by its interaction with the wave so that the resulting statistical distribution is the same. The droplet never exists in two places at once, and there's no randomness.
cues.zh: 液滴通过与波的相互作用而被推动，使得最终的统计分布是相同的。液滴从不同时存在于两个地方，也没有随机性。

cues.en: If there is any uncertainty, it's just due to our ignorance ignorance of what's going on. It's not that it doesn't exist. So pilot wave dynamics
cues.zh: 如果有任何不确定性，那只是由于我们的无知——对正在发生的事情的无知。并不是它不存在。所以导波动力学

cues.en: can produce many of the same results as quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 可以产生许多与量子力学相同的结果。

cues.en: Does this mean
cues.zh: 这是否意味着

cues.en: that this is really what quantum particles are doing?
cues.zh: 量子粒子实际上就是这样运作的？

cues.en: No.
cues.zh: 不。

cues.en: But I think it'll at least suggest that this is possible.
cues.zh: 但我认为这至少暗示了这是可能的。

cues.en: These are possible dynamics that could lead to the statistics which are captured in the quantum mechanical theory. And what's appealing about this is it gives you a clear idea of what's going on. You don't have to abandon the idea that the universe is deterministic and you get particles with definite position and momenta. I think it's great that we have two
cues.zh: 这些是可能的动力学，可以导致量子力学理论中所捕获的统计结果。这吸引人的地方在于，它让你清楚地了解正在发生什么。你不必放弃宇宙是确定性的这一观念，而且你得到具有确定位置和动量的粒子。我认为我们有两种

cues.en: competing theories
cues.zh: 相互竞争的理论

cues.en: for the same experiments.
cues.zh: 来解释相同的实验，这很棒。

cues.en: And they both ask you to accept odd things, just different odd things. And it comes down to what you're comfortable with really. Whether you prefer
cues.zh: 它们都要求你接受一些奇怪的东西，只是奇怪的方式不同。归根结底取决于你能接受什么。看你更喜欢

cues.en: the Copenhagen interpretation of standard quantum mechanics or a pilot wave theory.
cues.zh: 标准量子力学的哥本哈根诠释，还是导波理论。

cues.en: Let me know what you think in the comments. Do you like the pilot waves? I mean, it's definitely a very appealing picture.
cues.zh: 在评论区告诉我你的想法。你喜欢导波吗？我是说，这确实是一个非常吸引人的图景。

cues.en: Whether or not it corresponds to reality,
cues.zh: 至于它是否对应现实，

cues.en: that remains to be seen.
cues.zh: 还有待观察。

Now I know someone else who is pursuing their science goals this weekend that is Destin over at Smarter Every Day. He and I were looking at basically the same phenomenon, but he was looking at water droplets and why they don't coalesce. So if you wanna see how that works and how it works in space,
cues.zh: 该计划旨在激励人们更多地了解科学并追求自己的科学目标。我还知道这周末有另一位在追求科学目标的人，就是Smarter Every Day的Destin。他和我基本上在研究同样的现象，但他研究的是水滴以及它们为什么不会合并。所以如果你想看看那是怎么回事，以及在太空中如何运作，

cues.en: go check it out on his channel over at Smarter Every Day. And as always, thanks for watching.
cues.zh: 去他的Smarter Every Day频道看看吧。一如既往，感谢观看。

cues.en: Looking at only one frame per bounce, you can see how the droplets motion is guided by the wave it's effectively surfing on. And the wave remains even if the droplet disappears as happens sometimes if it encounters a little bit of dirt.
cues.zh: 每次弹跳只看一帧，你就能看到水滴的运动是如何被它实际上正在冲浪的波所引导的。而且即使水滴消失，波仍然存在——有时水滴碰到一点灰尘就会消失。

cues.en: What's really cool about this is the wave actually stores information about where the droplet has been. This is because every time the droplet bounces, it creates a new circular wave centered on its present location,
cues.zh: 真正酷的是，波实际上存储了水滴曾经去过的位置信息。这是因为每次水滴弹跳时，它都会以当前位置为中心创建一个新的圆形波，

cues.en: And that wave adds to the existing wave field on the surface.
cues.zh: 而这个波会叠加到表面上现有的波场中。

cues.en: So as the droplet moves,
cues.zh: 所以随着液滴移动，

cues.en: the waves it makes keep adding up, storing the information of where it's been. In fact, you can actually get the droplet to land on the backside of the wave. So now it's pushed backwards and it retraces its steps,
cues.zh: 它产生的波不断叠加，储存着它所经过的位置信息。事实上，你甚至可以让液滴落在波的后侧。这样它就会被向后推，沿着原路返回，

cues.en: erasing each wave it made previously
cues.zh: 并抹去它先前产生的每一道波

cues.en: one at a time.
cues.zh: 一次一道。
